To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) neural networks can be used to generate buy and sell signals for financial commodities traded in stock markets, (2) the neural networks are trained using a genetic algorithm, (3) the neural networks out-perform the efficient markets hypothesis in that they generate returns greater than those generated by random walk models, and (4) the neural networks generate returns significantly greater than those generated using buy and hold strategies.

1) Neural networks can be used to generate buy/sell points for a financial commodity traded on a stock market; 2) The returns generated using this methodology are significantly greater than those achieved on random walk bootstrapped data; 3) These results provide evidence against the efficient markets hypothesis, which predicts that stock prices follow random walks and that any returns generated by trading are due entirely to random chance.
